stances.claim: The Snyder v. United States Scotus decision (June 26, 2024, 6-3, Kavanaugh writing for conservatives, Jackson dissenting) 'practically legalized bribery' by distinguishing bribes (given BEFORE an official act to influence) from gratuities (given AFTER as 'reward or token of appreciation') under Section 666 of the US Code -- acquitting Mayor James Snyder despite his accepting a $13,000 Peterbilt check a year after Portage purchased five trash trucks from Peterbilt for ~$1.1M.

Kavanaugh's majority held that Section 666 is a 'bribery statute' requiring a 'corrupt state of mind' -- not proven in Snyder; left as a state, not federal, matter. Jackson's 22-page dissent retorted with a 'veiled swipe' that 'Snyder's absurd and atextual reading of the statute is one [that] only today's Court could love.'

CJ's 'simple mind cannot grasp and accept' the bribe/gratuity timing distinction -- 'In both, the purpose of the gift is the same -- to influence the public official into performing an official act according to the giver's direction. To me, it does not matter whether the reward or token of appreciation was given before or after the act; or a part was given before and the balance after. The act is a simple, plain, and shameful crime against the people.'
The Scotus produced 'a linguistic distinction that does not make a substantive difference' -- CJ 'cannot imagine our Supreme Court proudly posing' such a distinction.

Snyder is not isolated. CJ's June 17 column already documented Scotus practices -- 'unabashed acceptance of enormous sums as royalties, speaking fees, expensive gifts, paid vacations in exclusive hotels with private yachts and private planes, hobnobbing with the rich and famous in private clubs and, lately, partisan political bias' -- 'unethical, if not illegal.'
Closing escalation: 'Now, I am no longer dismayed. I am flabbergasted! The great chief justice John Marshall must be rolling in his grave.'

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with the 'dizzying political turmoil' in the US -- Biden's July 12 press conference 'miserably confused Russian Vladimir Putin to be the president of Ukraine, and Donald Trump to be the US veep'; his July 21 withdrawal-and-Harris-endorsement after contracting COVID; Harris's record '$150 million in campaign contributions in 24 hours.' The contest is now 'between a relatively young incumbent lady vice president, former US senator, and federal prosecutor with Asian descent versus a former president, Caucasian blabbermouth, and the oldest felon to seek the presidency of the most powerful country in the planet.' But as a lawyer and retired jurist, CJ is 'more befuddled by' the recent decision in Snyder v. United States (June 26, 2024) that 'practically legalized bribery.' The facts: James Snyder, mayor of Portage, Indiana, presided over the city's 2013 purchase of five trash trucks from Great Lakes Peterbilt Co. for about $1.1M; in 2014, Peterbilt 'cut a check for $13,000 to Snyder.' A federal jury convicted him of 'accepting an illegal gratuity in violation of Section 666 of the US Code,' rejecting his 'consulting services' defense; the district court sentenced him to 1 year and 9 months; the US Court of Appeals affirmed. Section 666(a)(1)(B) penalizes any agent of an organization or state/local/tribal government who 'corruptly solicits or demands... or accepts, or agrees to accept, anything of value... intending to be influenced or rewarded in connection with any business, transaction... involving any thing of value of $5,000 or more.' The Scotus, 6-3 (six conservatives appointed by Republican presidents -- three by Trump -- against three liberals appointed by Democratic presidents), acquitted by distinguishing bribes (given BEFORE an official act, 'inherently corrupt and unlawful') from gratuities (given AFTER as 'reward or token of appreciation,' which 'might be innocuous' or might 'raise ethical and appearance concerns,' with 'Federal, state, and local governments... drawn different lines'). Justice Brett M. Kavanaugh's 16-page majority held that Section 666 is a 'bribery statute' requiring a 'corrupt state of mind,' not proven in Snyder's case -- and left the issue as a state, not federal, matter. With a 'veiled swipe at the majority,' the 22-page dissent of 'neophyte Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson' sneered, 'Snyder's absurd and atextual reading of the statute is one [that] only today's Court could love.' Like Justice Jackson, CJ's 'simple mind cannot grasp and accept the Scotus distinction between money or gift given BEFORE and AFTER an official act is performed. In both, the purpose of the gift is the same -- to influence the public official into performing an official act according to the giver's direction. To me, it does not matter whether the reward or token of appreciation was given before or after the act; or a part was given before and the balance after. The act is a simple, plain, and shameful crime against the people.' CJ 'cannot imagine our Supreme Court proudly posing a linguistic distinction that does not make a substantive difference.' But perhaps he should not be shocked: his June 17 column was already 'utterly dismayed' at Scotus practices -- 'their unabashed acceptance of enormous sums as royalties, speaking fees, expensive gifts, paid vacations in exclusive hotels with private yachts and private planes, hobnobbing with the rich and famous in private clubs and, lately, partisan political bias' -- 'unethical, if not illegal.' Closing escalation: 'Now, I am no longer dismayed. I am flabbergasted! The great chief justice John Marshall must be rolling in his grave.'
